question.text: Who qualifies as a "new cadre distributor" for selling mutual funds?

answer.text: Retired government/semi-government officials, Class III and above or equivalent, with at least 10 years of service
Any person above the age of 60
Any graduate with a finance degree

explanation.text: The Logic: The new cadre distributor category includes postal agents, retired government/semi-government officials of Class III and above (or equivalent) with at least 10 years of service, retired bank officers, and other similarly notified persons. The Class III-and-above (or equivalent) qualifier and the minimum 10-year service requirement together define eligibility, and these distributors operate under Series V-B with a limited permitted product range. The Trap: Simply being above 60, holding a finance degree, or being employed by a private company does not qualify someone as a new cadre distributor — the source qualifier is retired from notified government/semi-government/bank/postal service at the specified grade or equivalent, with the 10-year service threshold. Note: When recruiting under this cadre, verify the candidate's grade (Class III and above or equivalent) and length of service against documentary proof — both conditions must be met, not just one.
